title: Quantum-Enhanced Phase Estimation with Photon-Added Even and Odd Coherent States in an SU(1,1) Interferometer
authors: Abdelmajid El Maaroufi, Mouad Ait Maskour, Bouchra Maroufi, Mohammed Daoud, Saeed Haddadi
abstract: We investigate phase estimation in an SU(1,1) interferometer employing $m$-photon-added even and odd coherent states as nonclassical input resources. The phase sensitivity is evaluated through intensity detection and the error propagation method, while the ultimate precision limit is determined from the quantum Cramér-Rao bound with the quantum Fisher information serving as the relevant metrological quantity. Our results demonstrate that photon addition significantly enhances the phase sensitivity, increases the quantum Fisher information, and reduces the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, leading to a clear improvement over the corresponding even and odd coherent states. Furthermore, the achievable sensitivity exceeds the standard quantum limit and gradually approaches the Heisenberg scaling with increasing photon-addition number. We also find that the $m$-photon-added even coherent states exhibit a modest advantage over their odd counterparts. As $m$ increases, however, this distinction becomes progressively weaker, suggesting that photon addition diminishes the role of the initial parity of the coherent state in determining the interferometric performance.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes quantum-enhanced phase estimation in an SU(1,1) interferometer using photon-added even and odd coherent states. The authors demonstrate that adding photons significantly boosts phase sensitivity, pushing performance beyond the Standard Quantum Limit. Crucially, they show that this photon addition mitigates the initial dependence of the measurement on whether the state was initially even or odd.
main_problem: The paper investigates how using photon-added even and odd coherent states enhances phase estimation precision in an SU(1,1) interferometer compared to standard coherent states.
main_result: Photon addition significantly enhances phase sensitivity, pushing the achievable precision beyond the Standard Quantum Limit towards the Heisenberg Limit, while also diminishing the initial dependence on the state's even or odd parity.
method: Phase sensitivity is analyzed using intensity detection and the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, quantifying performance via the quantum Fisher information.
model_or_system: The physical model is an SU(1,1) interferometer, which is realized using two Optical Parametric Amplifiers (OPAs) acting on input states, specifically photon-added even/odd coherent states and a squeezed vacuum state.
key_observables: Phase sensitivity ($\Delta\phi$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and the Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound ($\Delta\phi_{QCRB}$).
important_parameters: Photon-addition number ($m$), OPA gain ($g$), and squeezing parameter ($r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of specific nonclassical input states (PAECS/PAOCS) and models the interferometer using the SU(1,1) transformation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase sensitivity ($\Delta\phi$) vs. OPA gain ($g$) for varying $m$, comparing results to the QCRB, SQL, and HL. Other figures show the convergence of the performance difference ($\delta$) and total photon number ($N_T$) as $m$ increases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the metrological enhancement by comparing the performance of PAECS and PAOCS against standard coherent states, first using intensity detection, and then determining the ultimate limit via QFI and QCRB, concluding with the convergence analysis.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it explores using structured, nonclassical light states (photon-added states) to surpass fundamental measurement limits in an established quantum optical setup (SU(1,1) interferometer).
